title: Coefficient comparison for compactly supported direct image
statement:
Let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a morphism of standing schemes, $f=p\circ j$ a
compactification ($j$ an open immersion, $p$ proper), so that $Rf_!=Rp_*j_!$
([sk-thm-existence] (2)), and let $\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ be a listed coefficient map. For
$K\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ the composite
$$
\gamma^!_{f,K}\colon(Rf_!K)_{\Lambda'}=(Rp_*j_!K)_{\Lambda'}\xrightarrow{\gamma_{p,j_!K}}Rp_*\bigl((j_!K)_{\Lambda'}\bigr)\simeq Rp_*j_!(K_{\Lambda'})=Rf_!(K_{\Lambda'})
$$
is an isomorphism in $\Dctf(Y,\Lambda')$. It does not depend on the
compactification and is compatible with the composition isomorphisms
$R(gf)_!\simeq Rg_!Rf_!$.

proof.text: Write $T^V=(-)_{\Lambda'}$ and write $\delta_{a,M}:T(a_!M)\xrightarrow{\sim}a_!T(M)$ for [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback] (2). All schemes appearing in a compactification are standing schemes, hence qcqs, and their open immersions are quasi-compact ([sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]). Apply [det-sf-comp-coherence-single] to the compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}\overline X$ of $j$: it gives $j_!K\in\Dctf(\overline X,\Lambda)$, including finite Tor amplitude. Thus [det-prop-scalar-six-direct-image] (1) for $p$ makes $\gamma_{p,j_!K}$ an isomorphism. Composing with $Rp_*\delta_{j,K}$ gives the displayed $\gamma^!_{f,K}$. By [sk-thm-existence] (2), $Rf_!K\in\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$; [det-prop-scalar-six-ctf] (3) gives both $T^Y Rf_!K\in\Dctf(Y,\Lambda')$ and $T^XK\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda')$. Applying existence again to $T^XK$ puts $Rf_!T^XK$ in the same target category.

source.place: Isomorphism; the compactification-model lemma supplies the missing finite-Tor hypothesis

proof.text:
First consider dense compactifications $c=(j:X\to Z,p:Z\to Y)$ and $c'=(j':X\to Z',p':Z'\to Y)$ with $p'=ph$ and a proper refinement $h:Z'\to Z$ satisfying $h^{-1}(X)=X$. Write $e_{h,K}$ for [det-sf-comp-coherence-refinement]. The precise coefficient/refinement identity is
$$Rh_*\delta_{j',K}\circ\gamma_{h,j'_!K}\circ T^Z(e_{h,K})=e_{h,T^XK}\circ\delta_{j,K}.$$
Both maps have source $T^Zj_!K$ and target $Rh_*j'_!T^XK$. Identify the source with $j_!T^XK$ using $\delta_j$. By $j_!\dashv j^*$ and $j^*Rh_*j'_!T^XK=T^XK$, maps of this type are determined by their restriction to $X$ ([det-sf-comp-coherence-refinement] (1)). The right side restricts to the identity. For the left side expand $\gamma_h$ as the unit, pullback comparison and scalar-extended counit in [det-prop-scalar-six-direct-image]. Over $X$, $h$ is the identity, the pullback comparison is the identity comparison of [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback] (1), and the unit followed by counit is the identity by the adjunction triangle identity. The $\delta_j,\delta_{j'}$ restrictions are identities: they are the adjunction-conjugate comparisons of [def-sfb-derived-open-immersion-shriek-iso]. Thus the left side also restricts to the identity, proving the equation. Put $\phi_{h,K}=Rp_*e_{h,K}$. Naturality of $\gamma_p$ for $e_{h,K}$, followed by the composition formula $\gamma_{ph}=Rp_*\gamma_h\circ\gamma_p$ of [det-prop-scalar-six-direct-image] (2), now gives
$$\phi_{h,T^XK}\circ\gamma^{!,c}_{f,K}=\gamma^{!,c'}_{f,K}\circ T^Y(\phi_{h,K}).$$
This also covers replacement of an arbitrary compactification by its schematic closure: [sk-lem-nagata-density-normalization] identifies $j_!K=i_*j_{0!}K$ for the closed inclusion $i:Z_0\to Z$, with the identification restricting to the identity on $X$. The derived adjunction $j_!\dashv j^*$ stated in [def-sfb-derived-open-immersion-shriek-iso] makes it the unique such map, so the preceding displayed calculation applies with $h=i$; here $j^*Ri_*j_{0!}K=K$ follows by restricting the density-normalization identification. The compactification closures are Noetherian, since standing schemes are finite type over a field ([lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]). After this normalization, [prop-compactification-refinement] supplies common refinements of two compactifications. The scheme hypotheses hold because all maps are between separated finite-type schemes over the standing field. Normalize a common refinement to be dense. For either resulting proper map $h:Z_3\to Z_a$, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-section] says that $X$ is open and closed in $h^{-1}(X)$. Since $X$ is dense in $Z_3$, it is dense in this open inverse image; being also closed there, it is all of it. Thus $h^{-1}(X)=X$ as open subschemes, exactly the extra hypothesis of the refinement lemma. The maps $\phi_h$ are isomorphisms and transitive by [det-sf-comp-coherence-refinement] (2),(3), and [det-sf-comp-coherence-cocycle] identifies the comparisons through common dense refinements independently of that choice. The displayed commuting square for each refinement and normalization therefore proves independence of $\gamma^!$ for all compactifications.

source.place: Independence; explicit refinement equation and reduction from arbitrary to dense compactifications

proof.text:
Choose compactifications $f=pj$ and $g=qi$, where $j:X\to\overline X$ and $i:Y\to\overline Y$ are open. Compactify $ip$ densely as $\overline X\xrightarrow{j'}W\xrightarrow{r}\overline Y$. Put $A=j_!K$, which lies in $\Dctf$ by step 1. The statement [det-sf-comp-composition-interchange] gives $r^{-1}(Y)=\overline X$ and the unique isomorphism $\iota_A:i_!Rp_*A\to Rr_*j'_!A$ restricting to $\mathrm{id}_{Rp_*A}$. The coefficient-compatibility equation for this map is
$$Rr_*\delta_{j',A}\circ\gamma_{r,j'_!A}\circ T^{\overline Y}(\iota_A)=\iota_{T^{\overline X}A}\circ i_!\gamma_{p,A}\circ\delta_{i,Rp_*A}.$$
Both sides have source $T^{\overline Y}i_!Rp_*A$ and target $Rr_*j'_!T^{\overline X}A$. Under $\delta_i$, restrict them to $Y$. The right side restricts to $\gamma_{p,A}$. For the left side, restrict the unit/pullback/counit formula of [det-prop-scalar-six-direct-image] to $Y$: since $r^{-1}(Y)=\overline X$ and $r|_{\overline X}=p$, this is exactly the unit/pullback/counit formula for $\gamma_{p,A}$; $\iota_A$ restricts to the identity and $\delta_{j'}$ restricts to the identity on $\overline X$. Hence both restrictions are $\gamma_{p,A}$. This is an isomorphism by [det-prop-scalar-six-direct-image] (1), as $A\in\Dctf$. After identifying the source by $i_!\gamma_{p,A}\circ\delta_i$, both maps thus restrict to the identity of $Rp_*T^{\overline X}A$; uniqueness in [det-sf-comp-composition-interchange] (2) proves the equation. The normalizations of the $\delta$ restrictions are those of [def-sfb-derived-open-immersion-shriek-iso]. Apply $Rq_*$ to this equation. Combine the proper factors using [det-prop-scalar-six-direct-image] (2), and combine the open factors $j'_!j_!$ using the composition clause of [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback] (2). The two resulting composites from $T Rq_*i_!Rp_*j_!K$ to $R(qr)_*(j'j)_!T K$ are equal. On these compactification models, construct the canonical compositor as $Rq_*i_!Rp_*j_!\xrightarrow{Rq_*\iota}Rq_*Rr_*j'_!j_!\simeq R(qr)_*(j'j)_!$. Its first arrow is the isomorphism of [det-sf-comp-composition-interchange] (3); the last identification composes proper direct images and extensions by zero, with the same identifications used in [det-prop-scalar-six-direct-image] (2) and [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback] (2). The equality just proved is compatibility with this model compositor. This constructs the compositor used here directly for the admissible coefficients and standing field of the item. Step 2 identifies the comparison for this composite compactification with the one for any chosen compactification of $gf$. Consequently, if $\alpha_{g,f}:Rg_!Rf_!\to R(gf)_!$ denotes this compositor, the equality obtained is
$$\gamma^!_{gf,K}\circ T(\alpha_{g,f,K})=\alpha_{g,f,TK}\circ Rg_!(\gamma^!_{f,K})\circ\gamma^!_{g,Rf_!K}.$$
All its arguments lie in $\Dctf$ by step 1 and [sk-thm-existence] (2).
